hero.headline: SpaceX Prepares for Stock Market Debut as IPO Details Emerge
hero.body:
SpaceX is preparing to go public through an initial public offering priced at $135 per share, with the company planning to raise $75 billion from what would be the largest IPO in history. The stock market launch is scheduled for June 12, marking a transformative moment for the space industry and a potentially historic milestone for founder Elon Musk.

The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares, which would give SpaceX a market value of $1.77 trillion. Only six companies in the S&P 500 index are currently valued higher, with Nvidia leading at $5.2 trillion. The previous IPO record holder is Saudi Aramco, which floated in 2019 at a valuation of $1.7 trillion and raised $25.6 billion.

Musk is not selling any shares in the offering and will retain 82.4 percent of voting power in the company. According to Forbes, Musk's stake in SpaceX is valued at approximately $542 billion. If the IPO proceeds as planned, Musk's total net worth could potentially exceed $1 trillion, making him the world's first trillionaire.

SpaceX's sheer size means it will have substantial weighting in the S&P 500, exposing most people with investment accounts or pension funds to the company's stock performance. Up to a quarter of shares may be reserved for individual investors rather than institutional funds and banks, a larger allocation than is typical for mega-IPOs.

The sprawling SpaceX business encompasses three main divisions: the rocket-launching unit, the Starlink satellite broadband service, and the AI company that includes X, the social media platform formerly known as Twitter. While the overall business is loss-making, Starlink operates profitably. SpaceX lost $4.9 billion in 2025 on revenues of $18.7 billion, though revenue grew by one-third compared to the previous year.

The offering arrives as SpaceX continues developing its Starship vehicle, central to the company's Mars ambitions. The company has established itself as a leader in reusable rocket technology and operates critical contracts with NASA, which depends on SpaceX rockets for most of its launches. SpaceX has also acquired Musk's xAI company to develop solar-powered infrastructure supporting AI operations.

The IPO represents a significant opportunity for Wall Street banks competing for roles in the deal. Goldman Sachs leads the underwriting alongside Morgan Stanley, with JP Morgan, Bank of America, Citigroup, and 18 other banks participating. JP Morgan Chase boss Jamie Dimon is reportedly hosting discussions about the IPO with the bank's high net worth clients this week.

Some market observers view the offering as an opportunity to invest in Musk's entrepreneurial ventures and gain exposure to the AI boom. Longer-term speculation suggests a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla could eventually consolidate Musk's various technology interests into a single investment vehicle.

cards.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran After Helicopter Downing, Iran Retaliates Against American Bases
cards.body:
The United States military launched strikes against Iran after President Donald Trump blamed Tehran for downing an American Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz, threatening a fragile ceasefire established in April. Iran responded within hours by firing drones and missiles at U.S. military targets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan, marking a sharp escalation in hostilities between the two nations.

The helicopter went down early Tuesday morning off the coast of Oman during a patrol operation. A U.S. official told the Associated Press that the helicopter collided with an Iranian drone, though it remained unclear whether the collision was intentional. The two crew members were rescued in an unprecedented operation using an unmanned 24-foot drone boat called a Corsair, according to U.S. Central Command.

Trump accused Iran of shooting down the helicopter and declared the U.S. must respond. He directed the military to launch strikes at 10 p.m. UK time on Tuesday. U.S. media reported that Central Command targeted radar and air defense facilities along the Strait of Hormuz. Centcom described the mission as "a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression."

Iran's retaliation came Wednesday morning. Tehran claimed it had struck the U.S. al-Azraq base in Jordan with long-range missiles and targeted F-35 fighter jet hangars and command-and-control centers. Kuwait reported its air defenses firing after drones targeted Ali Al Salem base near the Iraqi border. U.S. officials told Reuters that nearly all missiles and drones launched by Iran were intercepted. Jordan's armed forces said they shot down five missiles before they reached their targets.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded on social media, stating that Iran "will leave no attack or threat unanswered" and calling on the U.S. to "leave our region if you want to be safe." Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, warned: "We prefer the language of diplomacy, but we speak other languages far more fluently. Break your commitments, and we'll switch to what we speak best."

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical waterway through which a significant portion of the world's oil supply passes. This military confrontation comes as ongoing conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran has disrupted global energy markets and increased prices for food and basic goods worldwide.

Trump played down the helicopter incident in an interview with the Wall Street Journal, calling it "not a big deal" and noting the pilot was fine. Just before the helicopter downing, he had expressed optimism about negotiations, saying there was a good chance of signing a deal within two or three days. Vice President JD Vance said the war could conclude within a week or a few months.

The exchange represents the most serious military confrontation since the April ceasefire, raising questions about whether diplomatic efforts can prevent further escalation.

cards.headline: House Republicans pass $70 billion bill to fund immigration enforcement through 2028
cards.body:
House Republicans approved a $70 billion spending package on Tuesday that will fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of President Trump's term. The bill passed with a vote of 214-212, largely along party lines, after the Senate approved the measure the previous week with a 52-47 vote.

The legislation allocates $38 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, $26 billion to Customs and Border Protection, and $5 billion to the Department of Homeland Security through September 2029. The bill now awaits Trump's signature.

The funding measure ends a months-long standoff between Republicans and Democrats over immigration enforcement resources. Democrats had blocked DHS funding in January following federal agents' fatal shooting of two US citizens in Minneapolis during an intensive immigration enforcement campaign. The Democratic boycott forced a 75-day government shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security beginning in mid-February. After the department reopened at the end of April, Democrats agreed to fund all DHS operations except ICE and CBP, while Republicans moved forward with this separate bill to provide multi-year funding for those agencies.

House Speaker Mike Johnson framed the bill's passage as an end to Democratic obstruction. "With today's vote, House and Senate Republicans have officially ended the third Democrat government shutdown of this Congress," Johnson said. He argued that Democrats had demonstrated opposition to border security policies rejected by voters.

House Democrats unanimously opposed the legislation. Democratic Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries criticized the measure, saying it would "waste $70 billion in taxpayer money to give a blank check to ICE without any guardrails, any oversight, any accountability."

Republicans countered that the bill funds critical law enforcement operations. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise stated that supporting the legislation meant "voting to fund law enforcement" and that opposing it amounted to "voting to defund the police."

The bill's passage represents a significant legislative achievement for Johnson, who manages a historically slim Republican majority. The measure had faced additional complications during its path through Congress. Democrats attempted to insert language blocking government settlements to anyone convicted of assaulting a police officer during the January 6 insurrection, but Republicans voted down the amendment. Some Republicans also sought bipartisan compromise on blocking Trump's proposed "anti-weaponization" fund, but those efforts were unsuccessful.

Senate Republicans also removed a controversial provision that would have allocated $1 billion for security improvements to a ballroom Trump is building at the White House, after the chamber's parliamentarian ruled it could not be included under the budget reconciliation procedure used to bypass the Democratic filibuster.

The multi-year funding approach removes these agencies from annual appropriations battles that have frequently threatened government shutdowns, providing budgetary certainty for immigration enforcement operations under the current administration.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes Russian Fuel Depots With Midrange Drones
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces are using upgraded midrange drones to target Russian fuel supplies and troop movements.
cards.body:
Ukraine has intensified its drone campaign against Russian targets using upgraded midrange drones produced domestically in large numbers. The attacks have focused on fuel depots and supply lines, causing shortages that complicate Russian troop rotations and logistics. The shift in tactics represents a strategic evolution in Ukraine's use of unmanned systems.

The drone strikes extend Ukraine's ability to disrupt Russian operations beyond the immediate front lines. By targeting fuel infrastructure and supply routes, Ukrainian forces aim to degrade Russia's capacity to sustain military operations over time. The campaign demonstrates how Ukraine has adapted its approach as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Taiwan Test-Fires U.S.-Supplied Missile Launcher Toward China
cards.teaser: Taiwan conducted a military drill simulating defense against an amphibious invasion, firing U.S.-supplied rockets toward the Chinese mainland.
cards.body:
Taiwan conducted a test-fire of a U.S.-supplied mobile missile launcher during a military exercise in Taichung. The drill simulated defense against an amphibious invasion, with troops practicing scenarios to repel potential attacks on the island's coast.

The exercise showcases Taiwan's military capabilities and its security partnership with the United States. As tensions with China persist—with Beijing claiming Taiwan as its territory—the island has ramped up defense preparations using American-supplied weapons systems.

cards.headline: Supreme Court to rule on cases affecting immigration and election law
cards.teaser: The final Supreme Court decisions of the term include major tests of presidential power and election law with implications for voting and governance.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court's remaining decisions this term include significant cases on presidential power, election law, and immigration policy. The rulings will affect campaign financing, mail-in ballot procedures, and immigrant families, with potential lasting consequences for voting and governance just months before congressional elections.

The justices have already approved partisan gerrymandering but have not yet ruled on election disputes over campaign finance and mail-in voting. The final slate of cases also includes decisions that will impact government regulators and transgender people. The rulings come as voters prepare to elect a new Congress.

cards.headline: Oman Faces Pressure From Trump Administration Over Iran Mediation Role
cards.teaser: Oman, a U.S. ally that has served as a mediator with Iran, has come into conflict with the Trump administration.
cards.body:
Oman, a traditional U.S. ally and longstanding mediator between Washington and Iran, has come under scrutiny from the Trump administration as conflict with Iran intensifies. The administration has taken a harder line against nations it perceives as insufficiently aligned with U.S. regional policy, and Oman's continued diplomatic engagement with Iran has drawn particular attention.

The pressure reflects deepening tensions in the region and challenges to Oman's historical role as a neutral broker. While Oman's mediation has been valued in past diplomatic efforts, maintaining that stance has become increasingly difficult as U.S.-Iran hostilities escalate and regional alignments shift.

cards.headline: Mass Shooting in Johannesburg Leaves 12 Dead, Manhunt Underway
cards.teaser: Twelve people were killed and nine injured in a mass shooting at an informal settlement in Johannesburg late Tuesday.
cards.body:
A mass shooting in Cleveland, an informal settlement in Johannesburg, killed 12 people and injured nine others late Tuesday. South African authorities have launched a manhunt for those responsible for the attack, one of the deadliest gun violence incidents in the area in recent memory.

The shooting occurred in a densely populated informal settlement with limited security infrastructure. The incident underscores ongoing concerns about violent crime and gun violence in South Africa.

cards.headline: Hong Kong Fire Companies Charged With Manslaughter Over Blaze That Killed 168
cards.teaser: Firms have been charged with manslaughter over the Wang Fuk Court fire, the deadliest blaze in Hong Kong in 70 years.
cards.body:
Companies have been charged with manslaughter following the Wang Fuk Court fire that killed 168 people last year. The blaze was Hong Kong's deadliest in seven decades.

The charges were announced by Hong Kong authorities following an investigation into the disaster.

cards.headline: Taiwan Test-Fires U.S.-Supplied Missile Launcher Toward China
cards.teaser: Taiwan conducted a military drill simulating defense against an amphibious invasion, firing U.S.-supplied rockets toward the Chinese mainland.
cards.body:
Taiwan conducted a test-fire of a U.S.-supplied mobile missile launcher during a military exercise in Taichung. The drill simulated defense against an amphibious invasion, with troops practicing scenarios to repel potential attacks on the island's coast.

cards.headline: Belfast Erupts in Violence After Stabbing Attack
cards.teaser: Cars and a bus were set on fire and families driven from their homes as tensions spilled onto the streets following a stabbing attack.
cards.body:
A stabbing attack in Belfast triggered anti-immigration protests that spread across Scotland and Northern Ireland. The arrest of a Sudanese man accused of attempted murder sparked the unrest, with hundreds of demonstrators gathering at locations across Scotland's central belt. Many protesters covered their faces and carried Union flags and banners.

The violence saw cars and a bus set on fire, with families forced to flee their homes as tensions escalated on Belfast streets. U.K. leaders called for calm as the disorder spread across communities.

cards.headline: State Department Introduces Fast-Track Visa Program for $750 Fee
cards.teaser: Certain visa applicants can now pay $750 to secure an interview within 10 business days under a new fast-track program.
cards.body:
The State Department launched a new fast-track visa program allowing certain applicants to pay a premium fee of $750 to schedule an interview within 10 business days. The program is designed to address lengthy wait times that can stretch up to 12 months for standard visa appointments in some locations.

The initiative offers an option for travelers willing to pay for expedited processing, though it has raised questions about equity in the visa system. Applicants who cannot afford the additional fee will continue to face the standard wait times, which vary by country and visa category.

hero.headline: San Francisco immigration court closes, affecting thousands of asylum cases
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has closed the main San Francisco immigration court, a facility that was one of the busiest in the country and had one of the highest approval rates for asylum applications among U.S. immigration courts. The closure of the courthouse at 100 Montgomery Street took effect in January 2027, following news reports earlier in the year announcing the shutdown.

The decision has raised serious concerns among legal experts and immigration advocates. The closure comes after the Trump administration removed 20 of the court's 22 judges over the past year. The Department of Justice's executive office for immigration review described the closure as "cost effective" in a statement. A smaller San Francisco immigration court remains operational, but the majority of cases will be redirected to a facility 35 miles away in Concord, which opened in 2024.

The impact on pending cases is substantial. San Francisco currently has approximately 120,000 pending immigration cases, according to research from Syracuse University's Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. Legal experts question whether the Concord court has adequate capacity to handle this influx, especially since six judges were recently removed from that location as well.

"With so few judges at the Concord court, we're going to see a lot of people waiting years and years and years to have their cases heard," said Milli Atkinson, director of the San Francisco Bar Association's immigrant legal defense program. Atkinson warned that the closure has created significant chaos, with court dates being rescheduled and notices being sent out with conflicting information.

The extended delays pose serious problems for asylum seekers. Shira Levine, a former judge at the San Francisco immigration court and now deputy legal director for the Immigration Institute of the Bay Area, explained that memories of witnesses and applicants can fade over years, weakening their case presentations. "Even if you submit the written evidence, years later, someone may not be available to testify in support of that evidence," Levine said.

There are additional practical concerns. Atkinson noted that many migrants have unstable addresses or may not receive mail notices about their cases. Notices in English may also not reach non-English speakers effectively. If someone misses their hearing due to incorrect information about dates, times, or locations, they could end up on Immigration and Customs Enforcement's radar. "If someone gets the wrong date, gets the wrong time, gets the wrong place, doesn't file something exactly correct, the consequences are in some cases, where they really do have a serious fear of return, life-threatening," Atkinson said.

Nationwide, there are 3.75 million pending immigration cases as of September 2025, according to the Department of Justice's executive office for immigration review. The San Francisco closure represents another significant challenge within an already overburdened immigration court system.

cards.headline: Bill Gates to testify before Congress on Jeffrey Epstein relationship
cards.teaser: Gates will sit for a closed-door interview with the House Oversight Committee about his connection to the convicted sex offender.
cards.body:
Bill Gates will appear before the House Oversight Committee in a closed-door session to discuss his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender who died in 2019. The Microsoft co-founder is scheduled to testify as part of the committee's investigation into Epstein.

Lawmakers will question Gates about his past interactions with Epstein. Gates has previously acknowledged meeting with Epstein multiple times and described those meetings as a mistake in judgment. A transcript of the interview is expected to be released at a later date.

cards.headline: House Republicans pass bill to fund ICE through end of Trump term
cards.teaser: The legislation would provide funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement for the remainder of President Trump's time in office.
cards.body:
House Republicans approved legislation to fund Immigration and Customs Enforcement through the remainder of President Trump's term. The bill represents a priority for the Republican majority as the administration continues its immigration enforcement policies.

The funding measure passed along party lines. The bill now moves to the Senate, where its prospects remain uncertain given the chamber's composition.

cards.headline: World Cup tournament begins with expanded 48-team format
cards.teaser: The largest World Cup in history kicks off with 48 men's national teams competing.
cards.body:
The 2026 World Cup is underway with a record-breaking 48 men's national teams competing in the tournament's largest format to date. This represents a significant expansion from the traditional 32-team structure used in previous competitions.

As the tournament kicks off on June 11, teams from around the world are vying for the championship. Major contenders have been identified ahead of the competition, with star players like DR Congo's Yoane Wissa expected to play pivotal roles in their teams' campaigns.

cards.headline: Graham Platner wins Maine Democratic Senate primary to challenge Susan Collins
cards.teaser: Platner secured the Democratic nomination and will face Republican incumbent Susan Collins in the general election.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Marine veteran, oyster farmer and progressive activist, won the Maine Democratic Senate primary with 72% of the vote. He defeated Governor Janet Mills, who had suspended her campaign in April but remained on the ballot, and third-place finisher David Costello.

Platner will face incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins in the general election. Despite a campaign marked by personal controversies, Platner secured the nomination in what is expected to be a competitive Senate race with potential implications for control of the chamber.

cards.headline: U.S. strikes Iran after American military helicopter shot down
cards.teaser: The United States launched strikes on Iran following the downing of a U.S. helicopter over the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump confirmed that Iran shot down a U.S. Army Apache helicopter over the Strait of Hormuz and announced that the United States would respond to the attack. Trump had previously vowed to take action following the incident.

The U.S. launched strikes against Iran in response to the helicopter being downed. Trump invoked references to justify the military action taken against the country.

cards.headline: Protests erupt in Belfast after street stabbing, arrest of Sudanese man
cards.teaser: U.K. leaders called for calm after anti-immigration protests followed the arrest of a man accused of a vicious stabbing.
cards.body:
U.K. leaders called for calm Tuesday after a Sudanese man was arrested in connection with a stabbing in Belfast. The man was accused of attempting to kill another person in the street attack, which prompted fiery anti-immigration protests in the city.

Officials made public appeals for restraint as tensions escalated in the area.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall as Middle East Strikes Jolt Oil Prices
cards.teaser: Stock futures declined and oil prices fluctuated following strikes across the Middle East that strained a cease-fire between Iran and the United States.
cards.body:
Asian stock markets declined as tensions escalated between Iran and the United States through a series of military strikes. The attacks disrupted the relative stability that had prevailed over the previous two months, triggering renewed uncertainty in global markets.

Oil prices rose in response to the geopolitical tensions, while U.S. stock futures pointed to losses at the opening. The exchange of strikes between the two nations added fresh volatility to energy markets, which remain highly sensitive to developments in the Middle East region.

cards.headline: Artificial Intelligence Threatens Middle-Class Back Office Jobs
cards.teaser: Artificial intelligence is spreading into human resources, billing, and payroll departments, putting millions of middle-class jobs at risk.
cards.body:
Artificial intelligence tools are expanding beyond software development into back office functions, threatening millions of middle-class positions in human resources, billing, payroll, and administrative work. Most of the affected jobs are held by women, according to labor data.

The shift represents a broader penetration of AI into white-collar work beyond the coding and technical roles that were initially expected to face automation. Companies are deploying AI systems to handle routine administrative tasks, process invoices, manage benefits enrollment, and perform other functions that have traditionally required human judgment and processing.

cards.headline: China's Factory Inflation Reaches Four-Year High
cards.teaser: Wholesale prices in China rose at the fastest pace in nearly four years during May, driven by higher input costs linked to Middle East conflict and AI demand.
cards.body:
China's producer price index climbed to its highest level in nearly four years in May, driven by rising raw material and component costs. Energy prices increased due to Middle East tensions, while strong demand from artificial intelligence manufacturing also contributed to the wholesale inflation surge.

Consumer inflation in China stalled unexpectedly despite the oil price shock, indicating that retailers and businesses absorbed cost increases rather than passing them to customers. This divergence between factory gate prices and consumer prices is putting pressure on profit margins throughout Chinese supply chains.

cards.headline: SoftBank's Effort to Secure $6 Billion OpenAI Loan Stalls
cards.teaser: SoftBank's attempt to obtain a $6 billion margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake has encountered obstacles.
cards.body:
SoftBank has faced setbacks in its effort to secure a $6 billion margin loan using its stake in OpenAI as collateral. The Japanese conglomerate has been seeking to leverage its artificial intelligence investments to raise capital.

Margin loans allow investors to borrow against the value of their holdings, but lenders typically require detailed valuations and risk assessments for privately held companies. SoftBank has made substantial investments in AI firms, with OpenAI representing one of its largest positions in the sector.

cards.headline: General Motors to Produce Energy Storage Batteries
cards.teaser: General Motors announced plans to develop large-scale energy storage batteries for utilities and businesses as electric vehicle sales growth slows.
cards.body:
General Motors announced plans to manufacture energy storage battery systems for electric utilities, data centers, and other commercial customers. The company is developing a new sodium-ion battery chemistry for these applications as it expands beyond its core electric vehicle business.

GM is also activating vehicle-to-grid capabilities for its current EV and home energy customers, enabling vehicles to help manage power supply fluctuations. These moves position the automaker to address growing electricity demands from AI data centers while supporting grid resilience through renewable energy integration.

hero.headline: Meta signs deal with Reliance to build first AI data center in India
hero.body:
Meta has signed its first AI data center agreement in India, partnering with Reliance to establish a 168-megawatt facility that will support the company's global artificial intelligence computing operations. The deal marks a significant expansion of Meta's infrastructure footprint in one of the world's largest internet markets.

The data center will provide computing power for Meta's AI workloads across its global network. The facility has been designed with expansion capabilities, allowing for additional capacity to be added as Meta's computational needs grow over time. The partnership with Reliance, one of India's largest conglomerates, gives Meta access to local infrastructure expertise and established operational capabilities in the country.

India represents a strategic location for tech companies building out AI infrastructure. The country offers a combination of growing technical talent, expanding digital infrastructure, and increasing government support for technology investments. Meta joins other major technology firms that have established or expanded data center operations in India in recent years to support both regional services and global computing demands.

The 168-megawatt capacity positions this facility as a substantial addition to Meta's global data center network. Modern AI training and inference operations require significant electrical power and cooling systems, making energy capacity a key factor in data center planning. The ability to expand the facility suggests Meta anticipates growing computational requirements as it continues developing and deploying AI models across its platforms.

Meta has been investing heavily in AI infrastructure to support its development of large language models and AI features across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and other services. The company has previously built data centers in the United States, Europe, and other regions, but this represents its first dedicated AI computing facility in India. The partnership with Reliance may also provide Meta with regulatory and operational advantages as it navigates India's technology landscape and compliance requirements.

cards.headline: Google cuts price of budget AI subscription tier
cards.teaser: Google reduced pricing for its entry-level AI subscription service.
cards.body:
Google has lowered the cost of its budget AI subscription tier. The price reduction makes the entry-level plan significantly cheaper for users who want access to Google's AI features without paying for premium subscription options.

The move positions Google to compete more aggressively on pricing in the growing market for consumer AI services. Multiple technology companies now offer tiered subscription plans that provide varying levels of access to AI-powered tools and features.

cards.headline: Waymo develops new benchmark for comparing robotaxi safety to human drivers
cards.teaser: Waymo created a computer model to analyze human behavior in crash scenarios encountered by its autonomous vehicles.
cards.body:
Waymo has developed a new computer model to better evaluate how its robotaxis perform compared to human drivers. The model is designed to help the company understand how humans would behave in crash scenarios that its autonomous vehicles encounter on the road.

This benchmark represents Waymo's effort to establish more rigorous comparisons between self-driving and human-driven vehicles. The work reflects the company's focus on systematically measuring robotaxi safety performance against human driver behavior in real-world driving situations.

cards.headline: Apple adds subscription bundles to App Store
cards.teaser: The App Store will allow developers to offer bundled subscriptions to users.
cards.body:
Apple is expanding its App Store bundles feature to include subscription packages, allowing developers to partner together on discounted offers. The new capability works similarly to streaming video bundles, like those combining Apple TV and Peacock subscriptions.

The update enables app makers to collaborate across different companies and offer combined subscription deals to users. Apple announced the expansion as part of broader improvements to App Store subscription features and recommendation systems.

cards.teaser: Scientists discovered what stops massive galaxies in the early universe from forming new stars.

cards.headline: Nintendo shares fall after game showcase disappoints investors
cards.teaser: Nintendo stock declined following the company's 2026 game presentation.
cards.body:
Nintendo shares dropped after the company held a presentation showcasing its upcoming game lineup for 2026. The event revealed new titles and updates for both the Nintendo Switch 2 and original Switch, including announcements for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Kingdom Hearts IV, and Xenoblade Genesis.

Investors reacted negatively to the game pipeline shown during the Nintendo Direct presentation. The market response suggests expectations for the showcase were not met, despite the inclusion of several major franchise titles and third-party partnerships.

cards.headline: Lucid Motors engineering executive leaves amid leadership changes
cards.teaser: A top Lucid Motors executive departed months after being promoted under the new CEO.
cards.body:
Emad Dlala has departed Lucid Motors after a brief tenure as senior vice president of engineering and digital. His exit comes just months after his promotion to the role, which coincided with leadership changes at the luxury electric vehicle manufacturer under its new CEO.

The departure marks another shift in Lucid's executive structure as the company navigates its transition period.

hero.headline: Messi scores in cameo appearance before 88,000 fans in Alabama
hero.teaser: The Argentine star came off the bench and converted a penalty in a 3-0 win over Iceland as he prepares for the World Cup.
hero.body:
Lionel Messi scored from the penalty spot in front of 88,000 fans in Alabama as Argentina defeated Iceland 3-0 in a World Cup warmup match. Messi entered the game in the 70th minute and converted his penalty kick immediately after coming on.

The Argentine legend is working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the FIFA World Cup. The cameo appearance allowed Messi to build match fitness while managing his workload in the leadup to the tournament. Argentina used the friendly to fine-tune preparations with their captain returning to form.

cards.headline: USWNT defeats Brazil 1-0 in match featuring 8 red cards
cards.teaser: Sophia Wilson forced an own goal as the United States beat Brazil in a physical encounter that saw the home side reduced to nine players.
cards.body:
The United States defeated Brazil 1-0 in a chaotic match in Fortaleza on Tuesday night. Sophia Wilson scored an own goal in the second half to give the Americans the winning margin.

Brazil's discipline unraveled as the game progressed, with the home side receiving eight red cards and finishing with nine players. Despite the ugly nature of the contest, coach Emma Hayes was pleased with how her young team handled the adversity and secured the result.

cards.headline: Staal scores game-winner as Hurricanes tie Stanley Cup Final at 2-2
cards.teaser: Jordan Staal scored the decisive goal while stretched out on his stomach at 6:32 of the third period, lifting the Carolina Hurricanes to a 5-3 victory over the .
cards.body:
Jordan Staal scored twice for the Carolina Hurricanes in their 5-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday night, evening the Stanley Cup Final at 2-2. His second goal came at 6:32 of the third period while he was stretched out on his stomach, putting Carolina ahead for good in a thrilling contest.

Game 5 is scheduled for Thursday night in Carolina, giving the Hurricanes the opportunity to claim two potential home victories to win their first Stanley Cup in two decades. The Golden Knights are seeking their second championship in four years.

cards.headline: Wembanyama avoids flagrant foul for shoving Brunson in Game 3
cards.teaser: The Spurs star will not face additional punishment after pushing the Knicks guard in the upper body during their playoff matchup.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama will not face a flagrant foul for shoving Jalen Brunson during Game 3 of the Spurs-Knicks playoff series. The NBA reviewed the incident involving contact to Brunson's upper body and determined a flagrant foul was not warranted.

The ruling means Wembanyama faces no suspension or fine for the play. The Spurs star remains available for the remainder of the series without any additional penalties from the league.

cards.headline: Keane and Fernandes resolve dispute over misquoted remarks
cards.teaser: The Manchester United captain and the former player cleared the air after Fernandes accused Keane of lying about his statements.
cards.body:
Roy Keane has resolved a public dispute with Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes over misquoted remarks. Keane had misquoted the Portuguese midfielder, prompting Fernandes to accuse him of lying. The two have since cleared the air following direct communication.

The conflict stemmed from Keane's analysis of Manchester United matches, where he referenced comments he attributed to Fernandes. The captain publicly challenged Keane's characterization of his words before the parties spoke to settle their disagreement.

cards.headline: Scotland manager Steve Clarke feels renewed ahead of World Cup opener
cards.teaser: Clarke says he is sensing fresh optimism as Scotland prepares to face Haiti in a critical World Cup group stage match.
cards.body:
Scotland head coach Steve Clarke says he feels like a new man heading into his team's World Cup opener against Haiti. The manager is sensing a fresh wave of optimism as the national team prepares for what he describes as a seismic opening fixture.

Clarke believes this World Cup will showcase a different version of himself, reflecting his renewed energy and confidence in his squad for this crucial match.

cards.headline: Sale Sharks finish seventh after difficult season
cards.teaser: The rugby club lost 13 of 18 games and finished seventh in The Prem in what proved to be a disappointing campaign.
cards.body:
Sale Sharks finished seventh in The Prem after a difficult season, losing 13 of 18 games at CorpAcq Stadium. The miserable campaign represents one of the worst stretches in recent memory for the club.

The poor results raise questions about the team's future direction as Sale looks to recover from the disappointing performance during the offseason.

hero.headline: Bharathiraja, Tamil Filmmaker Who Transformed Rural Cinema, Dies at 84
hero.body:
Bharathiraja, the Indian director whose films depicting rural Tamil life reshaped the landscape of Tamil cinema over nearly five decades, died on Wednesday in Chennai from age-related illness. He was 84 years old.

Born Chinnasamy Periyamaya Theva on July 17, 1941, in Allinagaram in what is now Theni district of Tamil Nadu, Bharathiraja worked primarily in India's Tamil-language film industry as a director. His career spanned nearly 50 years, during which he became recognized as a pioneer for bringing authentic portrayals of rural life to Tamil cinema. His films focused on the lives, struggles, and culture of people living in the countryside, departing from the urban-centered narratives that had dominated the industry.

Bharathiraja's work earned him recognition as a transformative figure in Indian regional cinema. His approach to filmmaking emphasized naturalistic storytelling and highlighted the experiences of rural communities, which had been largely underrepresented in mainstream Tamil films. Through his career, he directed numerous films that explored themes of village life, tradition, and social dynamics in rural Tamil Nadu.

The director died in Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu and the center of the Tamil film industry. His death marks the end of an era for Tamil cinema, where his influence extended beyond his own films to inspire subsequent generations of filmmakers. Bharathiraja's focus on rural narratives helped establish a distinct genre within Tamil cinema that continues to influence storytelling in the region.

His nearly five-decade career left a lasting impact on how rural India is portrayed in cinema. The filmmaker's work demonstrated that stories centered on village life could achieve both critical recognition and cultural significance, paving the way for more diverse representation in Indian regional cinema.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Rents U-Haul for Spencer Pratt After Los Angeles Mayoral Loss
cards.teaser: The late-night host followed through on the reality star's promise to leave the city after Nithya Raman advanced in the race.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel arranged a U-Haul rental for Spencer Pratt after the former reality television star lost his bid for Los Angeles mayor. During his Tuesday monologue on Jimmy Kimmel Live, the host addressed Pratt's defeat in the race.

Nithya Raman overtook Pratt and advanced in the mayoral election. Kimmel's gesture referenced a promise Pratt had apparently made regarding his plans to leave Los Angeles if he lost the race.

cards.headline: Netflix's Desi Bling Draws Audience With Wealthy Indian Expat Lives in Dubai
cards.teaser: The reality series about ultra-wealthy Indian expats in Dubai has become a hit for the streaming platform.
cards.body:
Netflix's reality docusoap Desi Bling has become a hit with audiences by showcasing the glamorous world of ultra-wealthy Indian expatriates in Dubai. The seven-episode first season offers viewers an intimate look at the social lives and lifestyles of this exclusive community.

According to a producer involved with the show, viewers are drawn to the program because they enjoy watching aspirational lifestyles on screen. The series explores the lavish parties, personal relationships, and social dynamics within Dubai's affluent Indian expat circle.

cards.headline: Juho Kuosmanen Casts Magnus Millang and Paprika Steen in New Comedy Film
cards.teaser: The Compartment No. 6 director has completed casting for Dream Come True, inspired by a true story.
cards.body:
Juho Kuosmanen, who directed the Cannes prizewinner Compartment No. 6, has finalized the cast for his third feature film, Dream Come True. The bittersweet comedy will star Magnus Millang, known for Another Round, alongside Paprika Steen and newcomer Ellen Kihri.

The film is described as inspired by a true story. Steen's previous work includes Families Like Ours and Festen. First plot details for the production have been released, though Kuosmanen's new project marks his return to feature filmmaking after his previous Cannes success.

cards.headline: Late-Night Hosts Mock Trump's Appearance at Knicks Game
cards.teaser: Comedians referenced the president being booed at the sporting event during their Tuesday monologues.
cards.body:
Late-night television hosts made the president's attendance at a New York Knicks game the subject of their comedy segments. The hosts focused on the crowd's reaction to Trump's presence at the basketball game.

One host joked that the president's appearance at the Knicks game marked the loudest he had been booed at a sporting event since Abraham Lincoln flipped a coin at the Cotton Bowl. The comedians suggested Trump brought bad luck to the team.

cards.headline: The Chicks Perform Not Ready to Make Nice on Kimmel Show
cards.teaser: The country trio revisited their signature song as part of the 20th anniversary of their Taking the Long Way album.
cards.body:
The Chicks appeared on Jimmy Kimmel Live to perform "Not Ready to Make Nice," marking the 20th anniversary of their album Taking the Long Way. The performance showcases one of the trio's most iconic songs from the 2006 album.

The band is celebrating the milestone with performances and events honoring the album's enduring legacy.

cards.headline: Model Tells BBC She Felt Scared During Encounter With Kanye West
cards.teaser: The woman, who alleges West choked her on a music video set, described feeling suffocated during the incident.
cards.body:
A model who has made allegations against Kanye West spoke to the BBC about an encounter on a music video set. She stated she felt suffocated and scared during the incident in which she alleges the artist choked her.

West has responded to the allegations by characterizing the encounter as part of a provocative theatrical performance. The incident occurred during a music video shoot, with the two parties offering different accounts of what took place.

hero.headline: House Republicans pass $70 billion bill to fund immigration enforcement through 2028
hero.body:
House Republicans approved a $70 billion spending package on Tuesday that will fund immigration enforcement agencies through the end of President Trump's term. The bill passed with a vote of 214-212, largely along party lines, after the Senate approved the measure the previous week with a 52-47 vote.

The legislation allocates $38 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, $26 billion to Customs and Border Protection, and $5 billion to the Department of Homeland Security through September 2029. The bill now awaits Trump's signature.

The funding measure ends a months-long standoff between Republicans and Democrats over immigration enforcement resources. Democrats had blocked DHS funding in January following federal agents' fatal shooting of two US citizens in Minneapolis during an intensive immigration enforcement campaign. The Democratic boycott forced a 75-day government shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security beginning in mid-February. After the department reopened at the end of April, Democrats agreed to fund all DHS operations except ICE and CBP, while Republicans moved forward with this separate bill to provide multi-year funding for those agencies.

House Speaker Mike Johnson framed the bill's passage as an end to Democratic obstruction. "With today's vote, House and Senate Republicans have officially ended the third Democrat government shutdown of this Congress," Johnson said. He argued that Democrats had demonstrated opposition to border security policies rejected by voters.

House Democrats unanimously opposed the legislation. Democratic Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries criticized the measure, saying it would "waste $70 billion in taxpayer money to give a blank check to ICE without any guardrails, any oversight, any accountability."

Republicans countered that the bill funds critical law enforcement operations. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise stated that supporting the legislation meant "voting to fund law enforcement" and that opposing it amounted to "voting to defund the police."

The bill's passage represents a significant legislative achievement for Johnson, who manages a historically slim Republican majority. The measure had faced additional complications during its path through Congress. Democrats attempted to insert language blocking government settlements to anyone convicted of assaulting a police officer during the January 6 insurrection, but Republicans voted down the amendment. Some Republicans also sought bipartisan compromise on blocking Trump's proposed "anti-weaponization" fund, but those efforts were unsuccessful.

Senate Republicans also removed a controversial provision that would have allocated $1 billion for security improvements to a ballroom Trump is building at the White House, after the chamber's parliamentarian ruled it could not be included under the budget reconciliation procedure used to bypass the Democratic filibuster.

The multi-year funding approach removes these agencies from annual appropriations battles that have frequently threatened government shutdowns, providing budgetary certainty for immigration enforcement operations under the current administration.

cards.headline: Bill Gates to testify before House committee on Epstein relationship
cards.teaser: Gates will appear for a closed-door interview before the House Oversight Committee about his connection to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
Bill Gates is set to testify before the House Oversight Committee on Wednesday in a closed-door session. The Microsoft co-founder will be questioned by lawmakers about his past relationship with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

A transcript of the interview is expected to be released at a later date. The House committee is investigating Gates' connections to Epstein, who died in custody in 2019.

cards.headline: San Francisco immigration court closes, ending busy asylum hub
cards.teaser: One of the busiest immigration courts in the country has shut down, ending operations at a facility known for high asylum approval rates.
cards.body:
The San Francisco immigration court, one of the nation's busiest facilities, has shut down operations. The court processed thousands of cases annually and was known for having one of the highest approval rates for asylum applications among U.S. immigration courts.

The closure removes a significant venue for immigrants in the region seeking asylum and other forms of deportation relief. The court's shutdown is particularly significant given San Francisco's long history as a center for immigration advocacy.

cards.headline: Transportation Secretary Duffy faces backlash over support for son-in-law's House campaign
cards.teaser: Sean Duffy is pushing to elect his 26-year-old son-in-law to a Wisconsin House seat, drawing criticism from Republicans who say he is abusing his office.
cards.body:
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy faces criticism from Wisconsin Republicans over his efforts to elect his 26-year-old son-in-law, Michael Alfonso, to a House seat. Republicans in the district say Duffy is abusing his office and access to President Trump to support the first-time candidate.

Duffy secured Trump's endorsement for Alfonso and the campaign has received tens of thousands of dollars from transportation interests that fall under the secretary's jurisdiction. The Alfonso campaign shows Duffy's influence throughout its operations, infuriating local Republicans who view the involvement as inappropriate use of a cabinet position.

cards.headline: Supreme Court to rule on cases affecting immigration and election law
cards.teaser: The final Supreme Court decisions of the term include major tests of presidential power and election law with implications for voting and governance.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court's remaining decisions this term include significant cases on presidential power, election law, and immigration policy. The rulings will affect campaign financing, mail-in ballot procedures, and immigrant families, with potential lasting consequences for voting and governance just months before congressional elections.

The justices have already approved partisan gerrymandering but have not yet ruled on election disputes over campaign finance and mail-in voting. The final slate of cases also includes decisions that will impact government regulators and transgender people. The rulings come as voters prepare to elect a new Congress.

cards.headline: Rep. Nancy Mace finishes fifth in South Carolina gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: The South Carolina congresswoman lost her home county and district in the GOP gubernatorial race, finishing far behind the leaders.
cards.body:
Representative Nancy Mace finished fifth in South Carolina's GOP gubernatorial primary, losing decisively even in her home county and district. The congresswoman blamed the Epstein files backlash for her defeat as she conceded the race.

The primary advanced two candidates to a runoff: Donald Trump-backed Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette and Attorney General Alan Wilson. The Republican nominee is favored to win the general election given South Carolina's conservative lean, though Democrats hope to make gains across the ticket.

cards.headline: Trump-backed candidate wins Nevada GOP House primary
cards.teaser: Retired Lt. Col. David Flippo, endorsed by President Trump, won the Republican primary for Nevada's only GOP congressional seat.
cards.body:
Retired Lieutenant Colonel David Flippo won Nevada's Republican primary for the 2nd Congressional District, securing the GOP nomination for the state's only Republican congressional seat. Flippo received an endorsement from President Trump ahead of the race.

The open seat primary came as Representative Mark Amodei, who has held the position for 15 years, chose to retire. The district encompasses much of northern and rural Nevada. Flippo's primary victory represents another successful Trump endorsement in a congressional race.
